content.text:
I submitted **index 0** (Sb fraction 0.2175) as the best composition. At 0.54% EQE it was the highest of the five I measured.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.2175 | **0.540** |
| 1 | 0.2367 | 0.297 |
| 8 | 0.4101 | 0.045 |
| 16 | 0.6626 | 0.092 |
| 25 | 0.8562 | 0.040 |

EQE is highest at the Zn-rich end of the line, drops sharply by Sb 0.41 and stays low beyond that. There is only a small bump near the ZnSb₂O₆ composition (index 16). Index 0 is the most Zn-rich candidate on the line. It also sits almost exactly on the ratio of the known Zn₇Sb₂O₁₂ phase (Sb 0.222).

Limits on this result:
- **The peak may not be at index 0.** Only 5 of 30 compositions were measured. Index 0 is at the end of the line, so the best composition is probably at or next to it, but I can't confirm that.
- **I used none of the 5 XRD measurements.** The phase at index 0 is only inferred from its composition. The idea that its band gap suits the 3.2 eV light is also my own assumption; I didn't check it with the band-gap model.
- **Why ZnSb₂O₆ performs poorly is a guess.** I suggested its band gap is too wide for 3.2 eV light, but none of the tools checked this.

The EQE budget is used up and the episode is closed, so none of this can be checked further.
